To install vLLM, you can use `uv pip` with the `--editable` flag for changes in Python code without compilation: `uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto vllm download-kernels`. For building from source, clone the repository and run `pip install -e .`. If you need to use a local version of cutlass, set the environment variable `VLLM_CUTLASS_SRC_DIR`. For CUDA 13.0, use `pip install vllm`. For ROCm, use `pip install vllm --extra-index-url`. For XPU, use `uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url --extra-index-url --index-strategy unsafe-best-match`.
To install vllm version 0.8.0, you can use the following pip commands to install the required dependencies: `pip3 install onnxruntime==1.20.1 pynvml==11.5.0 pyzmq==25.1.2 sentence-transformers==3.3.1 torch==2.5.1 torchaudio==2.5.1 torchvision==0.20.1 transformers==4.50.0.dev0 triton==3.1.0 vllm-nccl-cu12==2.18.1.0.1.0`. For conda dependencies, install `numpy 1.26.4`, `nvidia-cublas-cu12 12.4.5.8`, `nvidia-cuda-cupti-cu12 12.4.127`, `nvidia-cuda-nvrtc-cu12 12.4.127`, `pyzmq 25.1.2`, `sentence-transformers 3.3.1`, `torch 2.5.1`, `torchaudio 2.5.1
To install vllm, you can use the command `pip install vllm==0.23.0`. For the Ascend backend, you can use `pip install vllm vllm-ascend` once support is available. For now, you can clone the vllm and vllm-ascend repositories from GitHub and build the wheel from source. The sources do not provide a definitive answer for the current date's requirements beyond these instructions.

### vLLM Ascend Plugin. * [2024/12] We are working with the vLLM community to support [[RFC]: Hardware pluggable](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/11162). vLLM Ascend plugin (`vllm-ascend`) is a backend plugin for running vLLM on the Ascend NPU. This plugin is the recommended approach for supporting the Ascend backend within the vLLM community. It adheres to the principles outlined in the [[RFC]: Hardware pluggable](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues
If you only need to change Python code, you can build and install vLLM without compilation. Using `uv pip`'s `--editable` flag, changes you make to the code will be reflected when you run vLLM:

```
cd.
```

The install command will do the following:

1. Look for the current branch in your vLLM clone.
2. Identify the corresponding base commit in the main branch.
3. Download the pre-built wheel of the base commit.
4. Use its compiled libraries and `vllm-rs` binary in the installation. [...] There
Say, you are already inside rocm-vllm container (which you mentioned earlier), you make some changes in /vllm-workspace, you can run `python setup.py install`, which will do build vllm from source. Alternatively for easy experiments, you can change python code directly in vllm installation directory by showing where it is installed using command like "pip show vllm" without needing to run `python setup.py install`.
